findings.title: #936 AC2's "(and their reversals)" is never driven; the cell's own title asserts a reversal it does not create
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "A cell revises an accrual's amount and proves ... already-posted occurrences (and their reversals) are unchanged." The only cell is packages/db/tests/accrual-correction.test.mjs:169 p936.posted.untouched, whose title reads "an occurrence already posted under the OLD revision, AND ITS OUTSTANDING REVERSAL, are byte-for-byte unmoved". The scene never admits a reversal leg: line 172 asserts base.occurrence?.leg === 'primary', line 177 asserts before.length === 1, and the post-correction assertions are after.length === 1 plus deepEqual(after[0], beforeOcc). No clara.request_plan_catch_up call admits the reversal due event the way packages/db/tests/accrual-adjustments.test.mjs:450 p652.reversal.binds does, so no reversal occurrence row exists to compare. The cell proves the correction admits no NEW occurrence; it does not prove an already-admitted reversal survives a correction. The wave-3 WORK-ORDER addendum is explicit: "A door's behaviour is asserted only after it was driven. Do not write ... a sentence on screen unless a cell drove that door and saw it." wave3-lane06-ticket936.md repeats the title's claim as AC2 evidence.
findings.required_fix: Extend p936.posted.untouched (or add a sibling) to admit the reversal leg through clara.request_plan_catch_up and post it, capture the reversal occurrence row before the correction, then assert it byte-for-byte unmoved afterwards. If the reversal cannot be admitted in that window, strike the reversal clause from the cell title and record the gap in the report instead of claiming it.

findings.title: #936's headline defect stays reachable: an accrual-backed plan still offers the generic "Revise" control
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "Changing an accrual's amount no longer leaves the books contradicting themselves. Today the only way to change an accrual's amount is the generic plan revision door ... while the accrual's own detail row ... stays at the first revision." 0284's own header restates that divergence as the bug it closes. Measured on clara_l06: clara.list_accounting_plans carries no kind predicate (where p.client_id = p_client and p.firm_id = v_firm only), so an accrual's plan is listed; apps/web/components/plans/plans-list.tsx renders every kind (kindLabel falls through to the raw kind); apps/web/lib/plans/schedule.ts:233 planControls keys the revise control on STATUS alone; apps/web/components/plans/plan-detail.tsx:79-86 therefore still renders "Revise" for an accrual plan, linking to /plans/[planId]/revise -> PlanForm -> revisePlan -> clara.revise_accounting_plan (apps/web/lib/plans/api.ts:344). Nothing in the diff guards that route or that control. The DB half is legitimately constrained by lane 05/#908's pin on revise_accounting_plan, but the web layer is wholly this lane's, and no report line records the residual.
findings.required_fix: Either suppress or redirect the generic revise control for an accrual-backed plan at the web layer (planControls or plan-detail, with its own cell), or record the residual explicitly in wave3-lane06-ticket936.md under "what was deliberately left" with the follow-up ticket to file, so the integrator does not read AC3 as closing the defect the ticket's first sentence names.

findings.title: #986 AC2's "the basis's state shows which" is shown only in the transient 202 banner; the receipt relation is surfaced nowhere
findings.evidence: Ticket line: "The prior parse's targets are never left silently stale beside unread new content: they are retired and replaced, or explicitly re-pointed, AND THE BASIS'S STATE SHOWS WHICH." The retire-and-replace half is proved (p986.reread.refresh, re-run, pass). But clara.opening_target_refreshes appears in exactly three files on the branch: packages/db/migrations/0286_opening_source_reread.sql, packages/db/README.md and packages/db/tests/opening-source-reread.test.mjs. No read door returns it, apps/web/lib/registers/opening.ts does not select it (its column list at line 55 ends at created_at on opening_tb_targets), and no surface renders it. The only display of a refresh is the refreshedTitle/refreshedBody StateBanner in apps/web/components/registers/opening-parse-action.tsx:127-134, which lives in component state and is gone on reload. A person who refreshes and returns later sees only the current targets, with nothing on the basis saying an earlier reading was retired. The brief's out-of-scope line permits this work: it excludes only "any UI redesign BEYOND showing the refreshed target state".
findings.required_fix: Surface the refresh chain on the basis — a read of clara.opening_target_refreshes (SELECT is already granted to clara_authenticated and the policy is firm-scoped) rendered on the opening tab — or record in wave3-lane06-ticket986.md that AC2's "shows which" is met only at the moment of the act, with the follow-up to file.

findings.title: #986 restructures the pinned parse path (readOpeningParseSubject, openingTargetHandler) inside the delivery loop
findings.evidence: The ticket names the parse core and its (seed, document) key as "a pinned, load-bearing idempotency shape, so recutting it is a change of record, not a refactor", and asks only that the conflict stop being a dead end. The diff extracts readOpeningParseSubject out of parseOpeningTargets (packages/runtime/lib/opening-parse.mjs) and collapses both HTTP routes onto one openingTargetHandler factory (packages/runtime/src/openingRoutes.ts), rewriting every refusal return of the parse path into {refusal: ...} envelopes. WORK-ORDER rule 4: "Refactoring is not part of the loop; it belongs to the review stage." The change reads behaviour-identical — the 403 string interpolates to the same text for label='parse', openingOpKey is byte-identical with its pin cell passing, and the 17 pre-existing cells in packages/runtime/tests/wave-b-opening-parse.test.mjs pass — so this is a process note, not a defect.
findings.required_fix: No code change required. Name the extraction explicitly in the report as a refactor of a pinned path with its own regression evidence, so the integrator reviews it as one rather than as incidental diff.

findings.title: The correction form silently unsets a memo that happens to equal the purpose
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/accruals/accrual-correction-form.tsx draftFromAccrual seeds memo: basisMemo === row.purpose ? "" : basisMemo. clara._accrual_journal_basis defaults the derived basis memo to the purpose when none was stated, so a person who deliberately typed a memo equal to the purpose has it dropped from the successor row's stated particulars. The rendered basis memo is unchanged either way (the door re-derives it from the purpose), so the visible outcome matches, and the lane's own report flags the heuristic. Nothing in #936 asks for a memo heuristic.
findings.required_fix: None required at this altitude. Keep the follow-up the report already names (a top-level memo on clara.get_accrual_adjustment) so the pre-fill can stop guessing.
